question: Assume today is 2026-09-06. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of recreation visits to Yellowstone National Park in September 2026, as it will be reported in the National Park Service's official monthly visitation statistics.

target.what: Recreation visits to Yellowstone National Park as reported in the National Park Service's official monthly visitation statistics (NPS Visitor Use Statistics / Monthly Public Use Reports). A recreation visit is one person entering the park for recreational purposes; the same person entering multiple
target.publisher: National Park Service (NPS), Visitor Use Statistics program
target.cadence: Monthly, typically published with a lag of several weeks to a few months after the month ends
target.caveats: The target period is future relative to the 2026-09-06 cutoff, so no September 2026 data exist yet. The estimate must rely on historical seasonal patterns, recent 2026 monthly data (January–August 2026 if published before cutoff), and any available signals about park access, weather, or travel. The

candidates.hypothesis: September recreation visits in recent years (2019–2025) provide a seasonal baseline. The 2026 September value is likely to be similar to the same month in recent years, adjusted for any trend or unusual events. The ratio of September visits to the preceding January–August total can be used to project September 2026 from the known 2026 year-to-date total.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly recreation visits for Yellowstone National Park for September 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, and 2025; and the January–August totals for each of those years. Also the most recent 2026 monthly data (January–August 2026) if published before 2026-09-06.

candidates.hypothesis: Yellowstone's visitation may move with broader National Park System or Rocky Mountain region visitation. If NPS-wide or regional September visitation trends are available for 2026, they can indicate whether Yellowstone is likely above or below its historical seasonal pattern.
candidates.data_to_find: NPS-wide monthly recreation visits for September 2025 and any preliminary 2026 monthly data (January–August 2026) for the National Park System or for the Intermountain Region; also comparable parks like Grand Teton, Glacier, and Zion for September 2025 and 2026 year-to-date.

candidates.perspective: Entrance station counts and vehicle traffic
candidates.hypothesis: Recreation visits are derived from entrance station counts and vehicle occupancy factors. If entrance station data or traffic counts for Yellowstone in September 2026 are available (e.g., from park reports or traffic monitoring), they can be converted to visits using historical vehicle occupancy rates.
candidates.data_to_find: Yellowstone entrance station vehicle counts or total entries for September 2025 and any 2026 partial data; average persons per vehicle for Yellowstone in September; any real-time or preliminary September 2026 entrance counts.

candidates.hypothesis: Overnight stays and tours are a component of recreation visits. Occupancy rates and bookings for Yellowstone lodging and campgrounds in September 2026 can indicate whether visitation is likely high or low relative to historical norms. However, day-use visits dominate, so this is a partial signal.
candidates.data_to_find: Yellowstone lodging occupancy rates or reservations for September 2025 and 2026 (if available); campground occupancy; number of overnight stays reported by Xanterra or other concessioners; any forward-looking booking data for September 2026.

candidates.perspective: Park closures, weather, and access restrictions
candidates.hypothesis: Any closures, road construction, wildfire smoke, or policy changes in September 2026 could significantly alter visitation. Conversely, if no major disruptions are known, visitation may follow normal patterns. The 2022 flood drastically reduced June visitation that year, showing sensitivity to shocks.
candidates.data_to_find: News of Yellowstone closures or access restrictions for September 2026 (as of 2026-09-06); weather forecasts for September 2026; road construction schedules; any NPS alerts affecting park entry.

candidates.hypothesis: September typically accounts for a stable share of Yellowstone's annual recreation visits (e.g., around 10–12% in recent years). If a forecast for total 2026 visitation exists, or if the year-to-date total is known, the September share can be applied to estimate the target.
candidates.data_to_find: Historical September share of annual recreation visits for Yellowstone (2015–2025); any published forecast for Yellowstone 2026 annual visitation; the 2026 year-to-date total through August if available.

candidates.hypothesis: Online attention (Google Trends, social media mentions) for Yellowstone in September 2026 may correlate with actual visitation, but the relationship is noisy and not a direct count. It can serve as a directional check.
candidates.data_to_find: Google Trends interest for 'Yellowstone National Park' in September 2025 and September 2026 (if available); social media post volumes; website traffic to Yellowstone pages.

methods.rationale: Uses the only kept September level (2014-2018 average, p4) scaled by an explicit transfer ratio a1 to September 2026. This is a transparent level-times-adjustment route. Shared dependency: p4 is a 2014-2018 average, so it does not capture recent shocks or trends; a1 carries that uncertainty. Failure mode: if 2026 visitation is far outside the 2014-2018 range, the estimate will be biased.

assumptions.name: September 2026 visits relative to 2014-2018 September average
assumptions.rationale: The 2014-2018 September average is the only kept September level. Post-2018 visitation has generally been higher, but 2020 COVID, the 2022 flood, and possible 2026 conditions create wide uncertainty. A central ratio of 1.0 with a wide range reflects no reliable trend signal in the kept evidence.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to transfer the 2014-2018 September average to September 2026 when no recent September data are available.
assumptions.falsified_by: Recent September 2019-2025 counts or January-August 2026 data showing a consistent level materially different from the 2014-2018 average.

methods.rationale: Anchors on the only kept September-specific level (p4, the 2014-2018 September average of 663,651 visits) and scales it by a1, the assumed 2026-to-2014/18 September level multiple. This is a level-transfer route: it assumes the 2014-2018 September level is a valid base and that the recent upward shift is captured by a1. Failure modes: the 2014-2018 base may be structurally too low, and a1 is an assumption rather than a measured 2026 signal. Shared dependency: p4 is also the source of the seasonal shape used in m2.

A totals-times-share decomposition: projected 2026 annual visits (a3) times the September share of annual visits (a2). This route is structurally independent of m1's level-transfer logic, but it depends on two assumptions and on the 2026 seasonal shape resembling recent years. Failure modes: a3 and a2 are both assumptions, so the interval is wide; if September 2026 is unusually warm/dry or unusually smoky, the share will miss. Shared dependency: the seasonal-shape concept is informed by the 2014-2018 table (p4-p16), though the share value itself is assumed.

assumptions.name: September 2026 visits as a multiple of the 2014-2018 September average level
assumptions.rationale: The 2014-2018 September average (p4) predates the post-COVID surge and the 2022 flood. 2026 YTD is ~1% above 2025 and ~19% above 2021 (p34-p36), and recent Septembers have generally run above the 2014-2018 norm, but the level is uncertain and a bad-weather or smoke September could fall below it. A wide lognormal range centered modestly above 1.0 reflects that uncertainty.
assumptions.applies_when: September 2026 has normal access (all entrances open through Oct 31 per p1-p3) and no major closure, wildfire, or policy shock.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence of a September 2026 closure, wildfire smoke episode, reservation requirement, or published 2026 monthly data showing a level far from this multiple.

assumptions.name: September share of 2026 annual recreation visits
assumptions.rationale: The 2014-2018 table gives a 16.51% September share (p5), but recent years have shifted more visitation into summer and shoulder months, so the September share of the annual total is plausibly lower than the 2014-2018 value. No recent-year September share is available, so this is an assumption rather than a restatement of p5.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to convert a projected 2026 annual total into a September 2026 level; valid only if the 2026 seasonal shape resembles recent years rather than 2014-2018.
assumptions.falsified_by: A published 2026 monthly series showing September's share of the annual total outside this range.

assumptions.name: 2026 annual recreation visits at Yellowstone
assumptions.rationale: 2026 YTD through May is 773,653, up ~1% vs 2025 and ~19% vs 2021 (p34-p36). A full-year total near the recent 4.5-5.0M range is plausible, but no 2026 annual forecast exists in the kept evidence, so this is an assumption with a wide range.
assumptions.applies_when: Used only as the numerator for the September-share route; requires that the rest of 2026 follows a normal seasonal pattern.
assumptions.falsified_by: Published 2026 monthly data implying an annual total well outside this range.

This is a level-transfer route: it assumes the 2014-2018 September level is a valid base and that the recent upward shift is captured by a1. by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
